text: Once an Update Set is marked Complete, moving it to another instance follows a real, consistent path, the same four steps every time: export, retrieve, preview, commit.

First, export the Completed Update Set as an XML file from the source instance. Second, retrieve or upload that file on the target instance, which creates a brand-new, not-yet-applied Update Set record there -- nothing has changed on the target yet at this point. Third, preview it. Fourth, commit it, which is the step that actually applies every captured change to the target instance.

Preview is not a formality to click past on your way to committing. For every single captured change, it compares the version sitting inside the Update Set against whatever currently exists on the target instance, and it flags anything worth your attention -- most importantly, potential collisions, where someone changed that exact same thing directly on the target. Lesson 32 covers collisions and the other problems Preview can surface in real depth.

The direction never changes: Development, then Test or QA, then Production, always in that order, and Test is never skipped, even when a change feels small or urgent. Test exists specifically to catch exactly what Preview flags, in an environment where getting it wrong costs nothing, before that same Update Set ever has a chance to reach Production.

Skipping straight from Dev to Production defeats the entire point of having a tracked, reviewable promotion path in the first place. It's precisely the silent-copy risk the Instances & Environments lesson back in course two warned you about, just arriving through a different door.

Many organizations today also use Update Set batches, grouping several related Update Sets for one coordinated promotion, or increasingly Source Control and DevOps integration, storing configuration as code and promoting it through automated pipelines. That's covered properly later in this path, in the DevOps, Testing & Deployment course. Next up: the specific problems Preview can surface, and the real fix for each one.
